notes:
The two passes agree on every row, id, cell and disposition (all four checks kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only. One carried the case's priority and its assignee in two requirements, the other in one; both are changes to one row asked in one sentence, so they are one requirement here. One wrote the active cells on the skill and the rule as the predicate '= true', the other as the plain value true; the two are the same test, and the plain value is kept.
All four benchmark checks are conjunctions over several rows, so each is carried jointly by the requirements that test its parts: the insert check by the skill, user-skill, membership and rule requirements; the update check by the case and notification requirements; the whole-transaction check by all seven; and the join check, whose parts are looser forms of the same cells (user 83 holds skill 20 and belongs to group 1, rule 9 routes high priority to group 1, case 19 is assigned to user 83 in group 1, notification 19 belongs to case 19), by every requirement except the description. None holds on the seed. The case (hr_case 19) and its notification belong to org 19, while Tonya Garcia, IT Support L1, the new skill and the new rule belong to org 1, the acting user's org; the policy sets no rule on cross-org assignment, so the benchmark's values are kept. The acting user, Joanne Simpson, holds the manager role; the policy says managers cannot modify system configuration and lists assignment rules among the administrator's tables, so creating the skill and the rule could be refused under a strict reading. The file follows the request and the benchmark, which both expect every step done; a strict reading would turn the skill and assignment-rule requirements into stays. The case's skills column (JSON) is null on every seed case, so its storage format is not shown and no cell is written for it. The policy's short-description format (Service, Subject, Detail) and its 30-120 character limit are not tested by the benchmark and are left out. The update check's number predicate is dropped because the anchor hr_case_id 19 names the same row.
